brief.headline: Samsung/SKH major US deals inbound; Q3 DRAM/NAND inflation slowing but still up double digits; hyperscaler capex roars to $725B
brief.summary: <cite index="36-1,36-2,38-1">Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix set to announce major long-term memory supply deals with US tech firms during President Lee's Silicon Valley visit today, involving "very large" sums</cite>. <cite index="16-1,16-2">TrendForce projects Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ and NAND +10-15% QoQ, decelerating from brutal Q1 gains of 93-98% DRAM and 55-60% NAND</cite>. <cite index="8-3,8-13">HBM capacity fully pre-sold through 2026, with Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2 2026</cite>. <cite index="25-1,25-3">Hyperscaler AI capex hits ~$725B in 2026 (Amazon $200B, Google $185B, Meta $125B, Microsoft $120B), up 77% YoY</cite>. <cite index="27-11,27-2">TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap expected to narrow from 20% to 10% by end-2026 as monthly capacity climbs to 120-140K wafers</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025 vs Samsung at 22%</cite>, cementing SKH's structural lead. <cite index="5-3,5-4">UBS expects SK Hynix to maintain ~50% HBM market share in 2026 despite Samsung inching closer to HBM3E qualification and potential Nvidia pricing pushback</cite>. <cite index="6-1,6-4">YTD stock performance: Samsung +114%, SK Hynix +186%</cite>. Favor SKH on better HBM mix and qualification timing; Samsung faces qualification headwinds but broader logic/foundry diversification. Major US deals today could shift allocation dynamics—watch for LTA volume splits and pricing terms.

memory_cycle.stage: Late-stage upcycle with deceleration signals emerging
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="11-1,15-6">Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices expected +13-18% QoQ and NAND +10-15% QoQ, down from Q1's record 93-98% DRAM and 55-60% NAND increases</cite>. <cite index="8-11">Bank of America forecasts 2026 DRAM revenue +51% and NAND +45%, with ASPs climbing >30%</cite>. <cite index="8-5,8-7">HBM demand for AI infrastructure continues to tighten mainstream DRAM/NAND availability as chipmakers prioritize higher-margin products—"every wafer allocated to HBM is denied to PC/smartphone"</cite>. <cite index="9-1,9-2">Memory shortages expected through 2027, giving suppliers stronger pricing power than historical norm</cite>. Consumer demand softening (PC/smartphone) but enterprise/AI remains robust.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-1,5-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1 billion gigabits, driven by AI compute demand running ahead of forecasts</cite>. <cite index="8-2,8-9">HBM3E remains dominant AI memory through 2026 with pricing power intact; SK Hynix is only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and next-gen HBM4 at scale</cite>. <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects only "minimal to modest downtick" in HBM3E pricing for 2026 vs 2025 as more suppliers (Samsung, Micron) come online</cite>. <cite index="1-5,1-6,1-7">AMD MI400 featuring 12x HBM4 stacks with 432GB on-package memory and ~19.6TB/s bandwidth; early HBM4 modules deliver ~1.6TB/s each</cite>. Qualification risk for Samsung remains key watch item; any Nvidia LTA announcements today critical for 2H26-2027 allocation.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix to announce major US tech supply deals during President Lee's Silicon Valley visit
news_pulse.implication: Long-term memory LTAs with hyperscalers (likely Nvidia, OpenAI, others) could lock in multi-year HBM/DRAM revenue and validate supply discipline. Watch for volume commitments, pricing structures, and Samsung HBM3E qualification confirmation.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ—deceleration from Q1/Q2
news_pulse.implication: Pricing momentum slowing but still double-digit gains. Consumer pushback building as PC/smartphone OEMs resist further hikes; enterprise/AI demand remains inelastic. Margin trajectory still positive but deceleration flags potential cycle peak in 2H26.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 AI capex hits $725B (Amazon $200B, Google $185B, Meta $125B, Microsoft $120B), +77% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Massive demand tailwind for HBM/server DRAM persists. Capex-to-revenue gap (~$600B per Sequoia analysis) widening, raising ROI scrutiny, but spending shows no deceleration. Memory suppliers remain primary beneficiaries alongside Nvidia.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026; monthly capacity 120-140K wafers
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing faster than expected. More GPU/accelerator shipments possible in 2H26, increasing HBM attach rates. Nvidia dominates 60% of capacity; AMD, others competing for remainder. Risk: faster easing could shift bottleneck back to HBM supply.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix maintains ~50% HBM market share in 2026; Samsung HBM3E qualification still pending Nvidia approval
news_pulse.implication: SKH's HBM dominance intact. Samsung qualification timing critical—any announcement in today's US deals would be major catalyst. Pricing negotiations ongoing but Hynix expects only "minimal" ASP decline.

news_pulse.headline: Micron HBM3E 68% gross margin in Q2 2026; top-3 memory makers full HBM output pre-sold for year
news_pulse.implication: HBM profitability peak visible. Capacity allocation to HBM cannibalizing PC/smartphone DRAM/NAND, sustaining pricing power across product stack. Zero-sum game keeping consumer memory tight through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Memory stocks rally continues: Samsung +114% YTD, SK Hynix +186% YTD, Micron +141% YTD
news_pulse.implication: Valuation risk rising. Debate intensifying on whether AI has ended cyclicality or if over-investment/demand normalization triggers correction. TurboQuant and other inference efficiency advances cited as potential demand headwinds.

news_pulse.headline: Alphabet raises AI capex stakes in Q2 earnings; hyperscaler spending focus dominates Big Tech earnings week
news_pulse.implication: Amazon, Microsoft, Meta earnings next—capex trajectory #1 focus per CNBC. Any guidance cuts or ROI skepticism would pressure memory demand outlook; sustained/raised guidance extends HBM/server DRAM tailwinds.

brief.derivatives_signal: No derivatives or ADR data in payload; both 005930.KS and 000660.KS prices null. KOSPI, USD/KRW, futures all null. Monitor ADRs SSNLF/HXSCL for overnight US sentiment post-deal announcements.

Any hyperscaler (Amazon, Microsoft, Meta) earnings pre-announcements or capex guidance updates ahead of results next week
